title: The Marketing Mix
summary: The customer is the king of the market. The marketing mix is the combination of product, price, place (distribution) and promotion (the 4 Ps), mixed in an appropriate proportion to achieve the marketing goal: the right product, at the right place, at the right time and at the right price. All four decisions are interrelated, and the mix varies with resources and objectives. Price is the only element that generates revenue; the others produce cost; price is also the most flexible element.

A product is a bundle of benefits offered for a price (Stanton: a set of tangible and intangible attributes including packaging, colour, price and services; McCarthy: includes accessories, installation, instructions, package, brand name and after-sales service). Classification: (1) by use: consumer goods (convenience goods bought frequently without effort, shopping goods bought after comparison, speciality goods bought with special effort) and industrial goods (raw materials, machinery, components, operating supplies); the same product (e.g. coconut oil) may be consumer or industrial depending on use; (2) by durability: durable goods (used for months or years: refrigerator, car) and non-durable goods (consumed quickly: soap, salt); (3) by tangibility: tangible goods and intangible goods (services such as banking, insurance, medical treatment).

Components of the product mix: product characteristics (variety, quality, design, features, warranty); branding (a name, sign, symbol or design identifying a seller's goods; brand name is the part that can be spoken, brand mark is the part that is recognised but not spoken, trade mark is a brand given legal protection; benefits: product differentiation, differential pricing, easy introduction of new products); packaging (primary, secondary and transportation packaging; protects, identifies and eases handling; acts as a 'silent salesman'); labelling (name, contents, ownership, dates, grading and promotion).

Factors affecting price: cost, demand, competition, marketing objectives (profit maximisation, sales maximisation, market share, survival) and government regulation (Essential Commodities Act). Methods: cost-based (cost plus a margin), competition-based (going-rate pricing), demand-based (high price in high demand; differential prices such as cinema ticket rates), objective-based (penetration pricing: low introductory price to capture the market; skimming: high introductory price for status-conscious buyers) and sealed-bid pricing (tenders).

A channel of distribution is the route through which ownership and physical possession of goods transfer from producer to consumer or industrial user (Stanton). Functions: regular contact and information, transfer of ownership and delivery, financing through credit, after-sales service, assuming risks and placing orders. Types: zero stage (manufacturer to consumer; door-to-door, own outlets, direct mail; perishable and technical goods; Eureka Forbes), one stage (manufacturer, retailer, consumer; durable goods such as refrigerators, cars sold by Maruti through approved retailers), two stage (manufacturer, wholesaler, retailer, consumer; the most common for soap, oil, rice) and three stage (manufacturer, agent, wholesaler, retailer, consumer; for large, scattered markets).

Factors affecting the choice: nature of market (number, concentration and purchase size of buyers), nature of product (technical, value, perishability), nature of the company (financial resources, desire for control; a shorter channel gives more control) and middlemen considerations (experience, contacts, financial strength, margins).

The promotion mix is the blend of tools used to inform, persuade and remind customers. Advertising: paid, non-personal communication through media by an identified sponsor (print, radio, television, internet); flexible and low cost per head. Publicity: non-paid communication generating a favourable attitude (news items, press conferences). Sales promotion: short-term, temporary incentives to induce trial or purchase (discounts, free samples, contests, 'buy one get one free', coupons). Personal selling: face-to-face, direct presentation of the product to prospective buyers through oral communication. Direct marketing (direct mail, telemarketing, internet marketing) is also used. The main purpose of advertising is to increase sales and market share by informing and persuading customers.

objective: Which elements of the promotion mix are referred to? (i) It is a paid form of non-personal communication by an identified sponsor. (ii) It includes tools like direct mail, telemarketing and internet marketing.
(i) Advertising. (ii) Direct marketing.

(i) One stage channel. (ii) Zero stage channel.
October 2025

Give one word/phrase: (a) The component of marketing mix that relates to channels of distribution. (b) The component of marketing mix which persuades and influences the consumer to choose the product.
(a) Place (distribution). (b) Promotion.

October 2024
Which type of channel of distribution is suitable: (a) for a perishable product, (b) for durable products like a fridge?
(a) Zero stage channel (direct to consumer). (b) One stage channel (manufacturer, retailer, consumer).
October 2024
Classify as tangible or intangible: (i) cricket bat (ii) boarding a bus (iii) medical advice from a doctor (iv) pen.
(i) Tangible. (ii) Intangible. (iii) Intangible. (iv) Tangible.
Classify as durable or non-durable goods: refrigerator, salt, television, soap.
Durable: refrigerator, television. Non-durable: salt, soap.

Why are intermediaries used despite adding to cost?
They increase the efficiency of distribution by making goods available at convenient places in small quantities.

The part of a brand that can be recognised but not spoken, e.g. the arrow of Nike.
sa: Explain why promotion is considered necessary in the marketing mix.
A good product and price do not sell unless consumers know of them; promotion informs, persuades and reminds customers of availability, features and uses and arouses interest.
Explain why price is considered an important element of the marketing mix.
It is the only element that generates revenue, affects demand and profitability, is flexible and shows value.
Explain any three methods of price fixation.
Cost-based (cost plus margin), competition-based (going rate) and demand-based (price follows demand).
State any three factors affecting the choice of channels of distribution.
Nature of market, nature of product and nature of the company (also middlemen consideration).
Besides cost and demand, explain any three other factors affecting pricing.
Competition, marketing objectives and government regulation.
Product differentiation, differential pricing and easy introduction of new products.
Protects the product, identifies it, makes handling convenient and acts as a silent salesman.
la: Explain 'price' and 'promotion' as components of the marketing mix.

Price is the money charged; it depends on cost, demand, competition, objectives and regulation and is the only revenue-generating element. Promotion informs, persuades and reminds through advertising, publicity, sales promotion and personal selling.
Explain the factors affecting the choice of distribution channel.
Nature of market, nature of product, nature of the company and middlemen considerations with their cost.
By use (consumer and industrial goods), by durability (durable and non-durable) and by tangibility (tangible and intangible).
Explain the different channels of distribution.
Zero stage, one stage, two stage and three stage channels with examples.
Explain the components of the product mix.
Product characteristics, branding, packaging and labelling.
Advertising, publicity, sales promotion, personal selling and direct marketing, each with its meaning and use.
